name: Dynamic Rebricking
definition: A scheme where bricks are stored on disk in a large size (e.g., 256^3) but presented to the renderer as small bricks (e.g., 32^3). Small bricks are dynamically generated from large ones on request to balance disk performance (favored by large bricks) with early ray termination/empty space skipping (favored by small bricks).
summary: Dynamic Rebricking decouples physical storage from logical rendering size by generating small logical bricks from large physical bricks on demand, optimizing both disk I/O and ray-casting efficiency.
